heading: INT. HOLLOWAY FAMILY HOME - FUNERAL RECEPTION - DAY

units.text: INT. HOLLOWAY FAMILY HOME - FUNERAL RECEPTION - DAY
SERIES OF SHOTS:
-- A casserole dish passes from hand to hand down the hallway.
-- Black umbrellas drip in a brass stand.
-- A framed photo of GRANDMA LUCILLE on the piano, sunlight on the glass.
-- Cousins pressed together on the stairs, plates balanced on knees.

Joni Holloway, 40s, in a grey dress, ladles punch with a steady smile, while across the room her brother Jory Holloway, 40s, loosens his tie by the fireplace and Ames Okoro, 20s, their cousin, who uses they/them, drifts between the aunts with a tray, collecting cups, watching Joni and Jory the way someone watches two dogs near a bone.
There's more food in the kitchen. Please. Eat.
units.name: JONI

units.text: The room murmurs thanks.
Forks clink.
Eat. Sure. Like it's a holiday.
units.name: JORY

units.text: They said the will's being read after dessert.
units.name: AMES

units.text: Joni stiffens.
Jory doesn't.
-- LATER: The light has shifted.
Plates stacked.
Laughter.
Someone tells a story about Lucille's terrible driving, and for a moment the whole room breathes.
Remember the time she backed into the church sign?
units.name: JORY

units.text: She said it was in her way.
units.name: JONI

units.text: They laugh.
It's the first real laugh of the day.
Ames lowers the tray, relieved.
Then Ames's phone BUZZES.
ON PHONE (TEXT): did joni tell jory about the house yet
Ames goes still.
Joni notices.
Jory notices Joni notice.
What house?
units.name: JORY

units.text: Not here. Not now.
units.name: JONI

units.text: I think I'll get more coffee.
units.name: AMES

units.text: Sit down, Ames. What house, Joni?
units.name: JORY

units.text: The laughter dies out, one conversation at a time.
Everyone is watching now.
Grandma sold the house in March. To me. For a dollar.
units.name: JONI

units.text: Silence.
The clock on the mantel ticks.
